1	/**
     2	 * partials.ts
     3	 *
     4	 * Pure template-engine function for resolving partial inclusions.
     5	 * Supports {{> name}} syntax with up to depth-2 recursion to handle
     6	 * partials-within-partials. No file-system I/O.
     7	 */
     8	
     9	/**
    10	 * Resolve partial inclusions in a template string.
    11	 *
    12	 * Replaces `{{> name}}` markers with the content from `partialsMap`.
    13	 * Recursion is capped at depth 2 so that:
    14	 *   - depth 0 → 1: outer partials are expanded
    15	 *   - depth 1 → 2: one level of nested partials are expanded
    16	 *   - depth 2: recursion stops, marker is left as-is
    17	 *
    18	 * Each resolved partial is `trimEnd()`-ed to prevent trailing blank lines
    19	 * from causing double-blank-line artefacts during concatenation.
    20	 *
    21	 * If a partial name is not found in `partialsMap`, the original marker is
    22	 * preserved and a warning is emitted via `console.warn`.
    23	 *
    24	 * @param text       - Template string potentially containing {{> name}} markers
    25	 * @param partialsMap - Map of partial name → partial content
    26	 * @param depth      - Current recursion depth (callers should omit; defaults to 0)
    27	 * @returns          The template string with partial markers replaced
    28	 */
    29	export function resolvePartials(
    30	  text: string,
    31	  partialsMap: Record<string, string>,
    32	  depth = 0,
    33	): string {
    34	  if (depth >= 2) return text;
    35	  return text.replace(/\{\{> ([\w-]+)\}\}/g, (match, name: string) => {
    36	    if (!(name in partialsMap)) {
    37	      console.warn(`[WARN] Partial not found: ${match}`);
    38	      return match;
    39	    }
    40	    // Recursively resolve nested partials (depth + 1).
    41	    // trimEnd() strips trailing whitespace to avoid extra blank lines.
    42	    return resolvePartials(partialsMap[name], partialsMap, depth + 1).trimEnd();
    43	  });
    44	}

1	# Custom Variables & Dynamic Partials
     2	
     3	This guide covers two complementary mechanisms for injecting build-time content that varies
     4	across projects, suites, or individual personas:
     5	
     6	- **Custom variables** — inject template values via `BuildConfig.variables` and `SuiteConfig.variables`
     7	- **Dynamic partials** — inject or override partial content via `BuildConfig.partials`, `onPartials` and `onPersonaPartials` plugin hooks
     8	
     9	Both features follow the same design principle: **later layers win**. Values defined closer to the
    10	individual persona always take precedence over those defined at the global level.
    11	
    12	---
    13	
    14	## Table of Contents
    15	
    16	1. [Custom Variables](#1-custom-variables)
    17	   - [Level 1 — Global variables via `BuildConfig.variables`](#level-1--global-variables-via-buildconfigvariables)
    18	   - [Level 2 — Per-suite variables via `SuiteConfig.variables`](#level-2--per-suite-variables-via-suiteconfigvariables)
    19	   - [Variables merge/override order](#variables-mergeoverride-order)
    20	2. [Dynamic Partials](#2-dynamic-partials)
    21	   - [Level 1 — Inline partials via `BuildConfig.partials`](#level-1--inline-partials-via-buildconfigpartials)
    22	   - [Level 2 — Suite-scoped overrides via the `onPartials` plugin hook](#level-2--suite-scoped-overrides-via-the-onpartials-plugin-hook)
    23	   - [Level 3 — Per-persona overrides via the `onPersonaPartials` plugin hook](#level-3--per-persona-overrides-via-the-onpersonapartials-plugin-hook)
    24	   - [Partials merge/override order](#partials-mergeoverride-order)
    25	   - [End-to-end example — all four layers at once](#end-to-end-example--all-four-layers-at-once)
    26	3. [Combining variables and partials](#3-combining-variables-and-partials)
    27	
    28	---
    29	
    30	## 1. Custom Variables
    31	
    32	Custom variables let you inject arbitrary key/value pairs into the template context from outside
    33	the YAML metadata files. They are ideal for values that are known at build time but should not
    34	live inside the persona source files — for example, project-wide environment names, base URLs,
    35	or shared configuration tokens.
    36	
    37	### Level 1 — Global variables via `BuildConfig.variables`
    38	
    39	Set `variables` on the top-level `BuildConfig` to make values available to every persona across
    40	all suites.
    41	
    42	```ts
    43	import { build } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
    44	import path from 'node:path';
    45	
    46	await build({
    47	  suites: {
    48	    'engineering': {
    49	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/engineering'),
    50	      outputDirs: {
    51	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/engineering/vscode'),
    52	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/engineering/claude-code'),
    53	      },
    54	    },
    55	    'support': {
    56	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/support'),
    57	      outputDirs: {
    58	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/support/vscode'),
    59	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/support/claude-code'),
    60	      },
    61	    },
    62	  },
    63	
    64	  // Available in every template in every suite:
    65	  variables: {
    66	    company_name: 'Acme Corp',
    67	    support_email: 'help@acme.example',
    68	    environment: 'production',
    69	  },
    70	});
    71	```
    72	
    73	Any template in any suite can then reference these variables:
    74	
    75	```md
    76	## Contact
    77	
    78	Reach the {{company_name}} team at {{support_email}}.
    79	```
    80	
    81	### Level 2 — Per-suite variables via `SuiteConfig.variables`
    82	
    83	Set `variables` on a `SuiteConfig` entry to inject values that apply only to that suite. These
    84	override any same-named global variable from `BuildConfig.variables`.
    85	
    86	```ts
    87	await build({
    88	  suites: {
    89	    'engineering': {
    90	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/engineering'),
    91	      outputDirs: {
    92	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/engineering/vscode'),
    93	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/engineering/claude-code'),
    94	      },
    95	
    96	      // Override company_name for this suite only:
    97	      variables: {
    98	        company_name: 'Acme Engineering',
    99	        on_call_channel: '#eng-oncall',
   100	      },

   123	
   124	The `engineering` suite will render `{{company_name}}` as `"Acme Engineering"`, while the
   125	`support` suite will render it as `"Acme Corp"`.
   126	
   127	### Variables merge/override order
   128	
   129	Template variables are built from seven layers. **Later layers always win over earlier ones**:
   130	
   131	| Layer | Source | Priority |
   132	|-------|--------|----------|
   133	| 1 | `BuildConfig.variables` | Lowest |
   134	| 2 | `SuiteConfig.variables` | — |
   135	| 3 | `_shared.yaml` fields | — |
   136	| 4 | Per-persona YAML fields | — |
   137	| 5 | Derived/computed fields (`version`, `tools_list`, etc.) | — |
   138	| 6 | Cross-suite agent map (`agent_<slug>` variables) | — |
   139	| 7 | Target flags (`target_vscode`, `target_claude_code`, etc.) | **Highest** |
   140	
   141	> **Key rule:** `SuiteConfig.variables` overrides `BuildConfig.variables`, but is itself
   142	> overridden by `_shared.yaml` fields and per-persona YAML metadata. Use `BuildConfig.variables`
   143	> for project-wide defaults and `SuiteConfig.variables` for suite-specific defaults.
   144	
   145	For example, if `BuildConfig.variables` sets `env: 'production'` and a persona's YAML also sets
   146	`env: 'staging'`, the persona's YAML value wins.
   147	
   148	See [Template Syntax → Variables](template-syntax.md#variables) for the full reference.
   149	
   150	---
   151	
   152	## 2. Dynamic Partials
   153	
   154	Dynamic partials let you inject or override partial content without placing files on disk. They
   155	are useful for programmatically generated content, environment-specific snippets, and per-persona
   156	content that depends on runtime data.
   157	
   158	### Level 1 — Inline partials via `BuildConfig.partials`
   159	
   160	Pass an inline `partials` map to `BuildConfig` to register partial content as strings. This is
   161	the simplest approach when you want to inject content that is computed at build time.
   162	
   163	```ts
   164	import { build } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
   165	import path from 'node:path';
   166	import fs from 'node:fs';
   167	
   168	// Example: load a dynamically generated partial from an external source
   169	const changelogSnippet = fs.readFileSync('./CHANGELOG.md', 'utf8')
   170	  .split('\n')
   171	  .slice(0, 10)           // Take just the first 10 lines
   172	  .join('\n');
   173	
   174	await build({
   175	  suites: {
   176	    'my-suite': {
   177	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/my-suite'),
   178	      outputDirs: {
   179	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/vscode'),
   180	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/claude-code'),
   181	      },
   182	    },
   183	  },
   184	
   185	  // Inline partials — lowest precedence layer:
   186	  partials: {
   187	    recent_changes: changelogSnippet,
   188	    legal_footer: '> © 2025 Acme Corp. All rights reserved.',
   189	  },
   190	});
   191	```
   192	
   193	Templates reference them the same way as file-based partials:
   194	
   195	```md
   196	## Recent Changes
   197	
   198	{{> recent_changes}}
   199	
   200	---
   201	
   202	{{> legal_footer}}
   203	```
   204	
   205	> **Note:** Inline partials from `BuildConfig.partials` are the **lowest-precedence** layer. Any
   206	> partial with the same name loaded from `sharedPartialsDir`, suite-local `partials/`, or an
   207	> `onPartials` hook will override them.
   208	
   209	### Level 2 — Suite-scoped overrides via the `onPartials` plugin hook
   210	
   211	The `onPartials` hook runs once per suite, after all partials are loaded from disk and after any
   212	`BuildConfig.partials` map has been merged in. Use it to inject or override partials
   213	programmatically at the suite level.
   214	
   215	**Contract:** receive the accumulated partials map, return the (possibly mutated) map. The
   216	returned map is passed to the next plugin in the chain. **Always include all original keys** —
   217	return `{ ...partialsMap, myPartial: '...' }` rather than a fresh object.
   218	
   219	```ts
   220	import type { PersonaBuildPlugin } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
   221	
   222	export const environmentBannerPlugin: PersonaBuildPlugin = {
   223	  name: 'environment-banner',
   224	
   225	  onPartials(partialsMap, suiteName, suite) {
   226	    // Inject an environment-specific banner for every persona in this suite.
   227	    const env = process.env.BUILD_ENV ?? 'development';
   228	
   229	    return {
   230	      ...partialsMap,
   231	      env_banner: env === 'production'
   232	        ? '> ⚠️ **Production environment.** Treat all data as live.'
   233	        : `> 🔧 **${env} environment.** Safe to experiment.`,
   234	    };
   235	  },
   236	};
   237	
   238	await build({
   239	  suites: {
   240	    'my-suite': {
   241	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/my-suite'),
   242	      outputDirs: {
   243	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/vscode'),
   244	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/claude-code'),
   245	      },
   246	    },
   247	  },
   248	  plugins: [environmentBannerPlugin],
   249	});
   250	```
   251	
   252	> **Execution order:** Multiple plugins are chained — each receives the map returned by the
   253	> previous plugin. The order of `plugins` in `BuildConfig` controls which plugin runs first.
   254	> The **last** plugin to set a key wins.
   255	
   256	### Level 3 — Per-persona overrides via the `onPersonaPartials` plugin hook
   257	
   258	The `onPersonaPartials` hook runs once per persona (and per target), after `onBuildContext`.
   259	It receives a **shallow copy** of the suite-level partials map, so changes are isolated to the
   260	current persona — they will not affect other personas in the same suite.
   261	
   262	Use this hook when partial content depends on persona-specific data: role, tier, capabilities, or
   263	any field from the persona's YAML metadata.
   264	
   265	**Contract:** same chaining rules as `onPartials` — receive the map, return a new map. Mutating
   266	in place may work but is not guaranteed to be safe; always return `{ ...partialsMap, ... }`.
   267	
   268	```ts
   269	import type { PersonaBuildPlugin } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
   270	
   271	export const tierDisclaimerPlugin: PersonaBuildPlugin = {
   272	  name: 'tier-disclaimer',
   273	
   274	  onPersonaPartials(partialsMap, persona, context, suite, target) {
   275	    // `context` holds the post-onBuildContext merged state — all YAML fields
   276	    // and any keys injected by earlier onBuildContext plugins are accessible.
   277	    const tier = context['tier'] as string | undefined;
   278	
   279	    if (tier === 'admin') {
   280	      return {
   281	        ...partialsMap,
   282	        disclaimer: '> 🔒 **Admin persona.** Restricted to authorised users.',
   283	      };
   284	    }
   285	
   286	    if (tier === 'read-only') {
   287	      return {
   288	        ...partialsMap,
   289	        disclaimer: '> 👁️ **Read-only persona.** No write operations permitted.',
   290	      };
   291	    }
   292	
   293	    // Return unchanged map for personas without a tier field:
   294	    return partialsMap;
   295	  },
   296	};
   297	```
   298	
   299	A persona with `tier: admin` in its YAML will receive the admin disclaimer, while all other
   300	personas in the same suite receive the map untouched.
   301	
   302	```yaml
   303	# personas/my-suite/meta/admin-agent.yaml
   304	name: Admin Agent
   305	tier: admin
   306	vs_file_name: admin-agent.agent.md
   307	cc_file_name: admin-agent.md
   308	```
   309	
   310	The content template can then unconditionally include the partial:
   311	
   312	```md
   313	{{> disclaimer}}
   314	
   315	## Role
   316	
   317	...
   318	```
   319	
   320	Because `onPersonaPartials` runs per-persona, the `disclaimer` partial resolves to different
   321	content for each persona without any `{{#if}}` conditionals in the template itself.
   322	
   323	> **Isolation guarantee:** The builder shallow-copies the suite-level partials map before passing
   324	> it to the first `onPersonaPartials` plugin in the chain. Changes you apply inside this hook
   325	> are invisible to other personas in the same suite.
   326	
   327	### Partials merge/override order
   328	
   329	Partials are resolved in four layers. **Later layers always win over earlier ones**:
   330	
   331	| Layer | Source | Priority |
   332	|-------|--------|----------|
   333	| 1 | `BuildConfig.partials` (inline map) | Lowest |
   334	| 2 | `sharedPartialsDir` — files in the shared partials directory | — |
   335	| 3 | Suite-local partials — files in `<srcDir>/partials/` | — |
   336	| 4 | `onPartials` plugin hooks — plugin-injected partials | **Highest** |
   337	
   338	For per-persona rendering, an additional **copy** of the layer-4 map is handed to
   339	`onPersonaPartials` hooks, which can further override it for the duration of a single persona's
   340	render pass.
   341	
   342	> **Key rule:** `onPartials` hooks win over any file on disk. `onPersonaPartials` hooks win over
   343	> `onPartials` for the individual persona — but those overrides do not propagate back to the
   344	> suite-level map.
   345	
   346	### End-to-end example — all four layers at once
   347	
   348	The following example exercises every layer of the resolution order in a single `build()` call.
   349	It mirrors the integration test suite added in the WP-008 test coverage pass, so you can compare
   350	the example code with the live tests in `tests/integration/build.test.ts`.
   351	
   352	**Scenario:** two personas share a template that includes `{{> dynamic_partial}}`. Each layer adds
   353	or overrides the partial, and the highest-precedence layer wins.
   354	
   355	```ts
   356	import { build } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
   357	import type { PersonaBuildPlugin } from '@mistralys/persona-builder';
   358	import path from 'node:path';
   359	
   360	// ----- Layer 4: onPersonaPartials — per-persona override (highest precedence) -----
   361	// Demonstrates the per-persona isolation guarantee: each persona receives
   362	// distinct partial content; changes for one persona never affect another.
   363	const perPersonaPlugin: PersonaBuildPlugin = {
   364	  name: 'per-persona-partial',
   365	
   366	  onPersonaPartials(partialsMap, persona) {
   367	    // The builder already shallow-copied the suite-level map before calling
   368	    // this hook, so mutations here are invisible to other personas.
   369	    return {
   370	      ...partialsMap,
   371	      dynamic_partial: `Content tailored for ${persona.name}.`,
   372	    };
   373	  },
   374	};
   375	
   376	// ----- Layer 3: onPartials — suite-level override -----
   377	// Runs once per suite after file-based partials are loaded.
   378	// Wins over any file on disk; loses to onPersonaPartials.
   379	const suitePlugin: PersonaBuildPlugin = {
   380	  name: 'suite-partial',
   381	
   382	  onPartials(partialsMap) {
   383	    return {
   384	      ...partialsMap,
   385	      dynamic_partial: 'Suite-level content (overrides disk files).',
   386	    };
   387	  },
   388	};
   389	
   390	await build({
   391	  suites: {
   392	    'my-suite': {
   393	      srcDir: path.resolve('./personas/my-suite'),
   394	      // Layer 3 (suite-local files): any .md file in ./personas/my-suite/partials/
   395	      // named dynamic_partial.md would be layer 3 — overridden by onPartials.
   396	      outputDirs: {
   397	        vscode: path.resolve('./dist/vscode'),
   398	        'claude-code': path.resolve('./dist/claude-code'),
   399	      },
   400	    },

   417	**Resolution outcome for each persona** (highest-precedence layer wins):
   418	
   419	| Layer | Source | Value of `dynamic_partial` | Wins? |
   420	|-------|--------|---------------------------|-------|
   421	| 1 | `BuildConfig.partials` | `'Fallback content from BuildConfig.partials.'` | No |
   422	| 2 | `sharedPartialsDir` file | _(value from file, if present)_ | No |
   423	| 3 | `onPartials` hook | `'Suite-level content (overrides disk files).'` | No |

   430	---
   431	
   432	## 3. Combining variables and partials
   433	
   434	Variables and partials compose naturally. A partial injected by `onPersonaPartials` can itself
   435	reference template variables, and those variables are resolved in the normal 7-layer merge after
   436	all partials have been resolved.
   437	
   438	```ts
   439	// Plugin: inject a partial that references a template variable
   440	export const signaturePlugin: PersonaBuildPlugin = {
   441	  name: 'signature',
   442	
   443	  onPersonaPartials(partialsMap, persona, context) {
   444	    // The partial content can use {{variable}} syntax —
   445	    // variable substitution runs after partial inclusion.
   446	    return {
   447	      ...partialsMap,
   448	      signature: '— {{name}} v{{version}}, brought to you by {{company_name}}',
   449	    };
   450	  },
   451	};
   452	```
   453	
   454	Processing order for a template that includes `{{> signature}}`:
   455	
   456	1. `{{> signature}}` is replaced with the partial's raw content string.
   457	2. Template conditionals (`{{#if … }}`) are evaluated.
   458	3. `{{name}}`, `{{version}}`, and `{{company_name}}` are substituted from the merged context.
   459	
   460	This means you can author generic, reusable partial templates that are parameterised by context
   461	variables — the combination lets you express sophisticated per-persona content without hard-coding
   462	anything in the plugin itself.
   463	
   464	---

   470	- [Template Syntax](template-syntax.md) — variable substitution and partial inclusion

   329	Partials are resolved in four layers. **Later layers always win over earlier ones**:
   330	
   331	| Layer | Source | Priority |
   332	|-------|--------|----------|
   333	| 1 | `BuildConfig.partials` (inline map) | Lowest |
   334	| 2 | `sharedPartialsDir` — files in the shared partials directory | — |
   335	| 3 | Suite-local partials — files in `<srcDir>/partials/` | — |
   336	| 4 | `onPartials` plugin hooks — plugin-injected partials | **Highest** |
   337	
   338	For per-persona rendering, an additional **copy** of the layer-4 map is handed to
   339	`onPersonaPartials` hooks, which can further override it for the duration of a single persona's
   340	render pass.
   341	
   342	> **Key rule:** `onPartials` hooks win over any file on disk. `onPersonaPartials` hooks win over
   343	> `onPartials` for the individual persona — but those overrides do not propagate back to the
   344	> suite-level map.
   345	
   346	> **Nesting limit:** Partial inclusion is resolved with a maximum recursion depth of **2**. This
   347	> means a partial can itself include one level of nested partials (i.e. a partial-within-a-partial),
   348	> but a third level of nesting is **not** expanded — the `{{> name}}` marker is left as-is in the
   349	> output. This cap applies to all four layers, including partials injected by `onPartials` and
   350	> `onPersonaPartials` hooks. If you encounter unexpanded `{{> …}}` markers in your output, check
   351	> whether your partials are nested more than two levels deep.
